seed: how to find new music, discovery, tools, services, radio
note: This is not a genre guide. The canon is discovery services and tools that the article cannot omit, not records. `embed_id` appears only for services with embedded players (radio shows).

required_records.title: Every Noise at Once
required_records.why: article feature: 'Every Noise at Once aggregates critic and user scores across publications and is a fast way to see what a year looked like from outside your own listening.' Named as a primary tool for music discovery

required_records.title: Bandcamp
required_records.why: article feature: dedicated Bandcamp section with multiple references. The page opens with 'Bandcamp is the only place left where you can bet on an artist you have never heard of.' Central to independent music discovery

required_records.title: Discogs
required_records.why: article feature: alongside RateYourMusic in the databases section as canonical for collecting and discovery. 'Discogs and RateYourMusic are the two places people actually go to read about records.'

required_records.title: RateYourMusic
required_records.why: article feature: paired with Discogs as essential database for record discovery and cultural mood. 'RateYourMusic is where you see what people are arguing about.'

required_records.title: NTS Radio
required_records.why: article feature: opening line of the radio section: 'NTS Radio is the one most often named.' Described as the reference point for online community radio. Has embedded Spotify show player.

required_records.title: Boiler Room
required_records.why: article feature: 'The place to find them is YouTube, where Boiler Room, HÖR, Cercle, Dekmantel, Keep Hush and every radio station above upload full recordings.' Named as canonical DJ set platform

required_records.title: Album of the Year
required_records.why: article feature: 'Album of the Year aggregates critic and user scores across publications and is a fast way to see what a year looked like from outside your own listening. End-of-year lists are best read the following spring.'

known_gaps.title: Rinse FM, The Lot Radio, Kiosk Radio, Seoul Community Radio, Manila Community Radio, Radio Rudina, Boxout.fm
known_gaps.why: source: article. 'Then there are the ones nobody outside their city talks about, and this is where it gets interesting. Kiosk Radio broadcasts from a wooden shack in a Brussels park. Seoul Community Radio, Bangkok Community Radio, Manila Community Radio, Radio Rudina in the Balkans and Boxout.fm in Delhi all do the same job for their own scenes.' These stations are named to make the argument about geography but have no player embeds to demonstrate the claim

known_gaps.title: Genius.com, Genius annotations
known_gaps.why: mentioned in the article context ('Genius is the place you read other people's interpretations of the lyrics') but not in a feature-level way; may be intentionally low-profile
